packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-13 - unverified first reading from images only

Exposure / method notes
- No identification of the work or author was revealed to me. Visible modern pencil labels on the parchment read approximately "Stams, StA, Fragm. 25r" (face 1, right margin) and "Stams, StA, Fragm. 25v" (face 2, left margin). The directory name contains "stams". These are holding labels only, and I did not use them to identify the text.
- I used no tools other than viewing the six images. (For packet-15 I made enlarged crops. I made none here.) All six images loaded.

Layout survey (observations)
- image-001 = overview of face 1. image-002 (upper) and image-003 (lower) = native tiles of face 1. image-004 = overview of face 2. image-005 (upper) and image-006 (lower) = native tiles of face 2.
- A single rectangular fragment (c. 7 x 13 cm on the scale) holding one column of text, ruled with vertical bounding lines. About 29 lines survive per face. The top and bottom are trimmed, with partial lines at both edges.
- Gothic book hand in dark brown ink, with red for rubrics, red underlining of citations, and red strokes on capitals.
- Face 1: the surviving column has letter traces of a neighbouring column in the far left margin (line-ends of another column, mostly trimmed away). It has one red rubric line, a large red initial S (c. 6 lines high), and a red-underlined citation line.
- Face 2: there are letter traces of a neighbouring column at the far right edge. It has a red rubric, a very tall red initial I (c. 10+ lines), and a numbered sequence of capitals touched in red (Primo, Secundum, Tercium, ...).
- Tentative: sermon or preaching prose. Face 1 contains a red rubric that looks like a sermon heading ("S(er)mo de animab(us)"?). Face 2 has an enumerated list followed by a second enumerated list.

Selected spans: I read all surviving lines on both faces. Unread: the trimmed neighbouring-column traces (only single letters survive) and the partial lines at the top and bottom edges.
Overlap: image-003 lines 1-4 repeat image-002 lines 13-16. image-006 lines 1-4 repeat image-005 lines 13-16. I transcribe the overlap once and flag it.

Right edge of face 2 (another column, trimmed): isolated letters, e.g. "t", "la", next to image-006 l.6-17. Not readable.

Limitations
- Top and bottom lines are trimmed. The neighbouring columns survive only as single letters at the edges.
- Several abbreviations are uncertain and marked with "?". These include "sbuemete" (face 1), the middles of image-003 l.9-10 and l.16, and image-005 l.5.
- Which face is recto is not determinable from these images.
- A crop that includes the trimmed margins at higher magnification might recover a few words of the adjacent columns.
